name: basic.json
description: Basic rule set for auditing AWS environments

rules.name: IAM User MFA Token
rules.description: IAM Users should have MFA enabled
rules.remediation: Enable MFA for the IAM user to enhance security.

rules.name: IAM User Access Keys
rules.description: Access Keys should not be used for IAM Users. Instead use IAM Identity Center to setup Single Sign-on.
rules.remediation: Remove access keys and use IAM Identity Center for Single Sign-on.

rules.name: IAM User Inline Policies
rules.description: IAM Users should not have inline IAM policies. Instead use IAM Groups to define IAM Policies and assign the user to the group.
rules.remediation: Remove inline policies and use IAM Groups instead.

rules.name: IAM User Attached Policies
rules.description: IAM Policies should not be attached to IAM Users. Instead use IAM Groups to define IAM Policies and assign the user to the group.
rules.remediation: Remove attached policies and use IAM Groups instead.

rules.name: IAM User Not in Groups
rules.description: IAM Users should be assigned to IAM Groups for better policy management
rules.remediation: Add the user to an IAM group that carries the permissions they need, then remove any policies attached directly to the user. Group membership is far easier to review than per-user grants when someone changes role or leaves.

rules.name: IAM Role Inline Policies
rules.description: IAM Roles should not have inline IAM policies. Instead use managed policies or customer managed policies.
rules.remediation: Replace the inline role policy with a customer managed policy: copy the policy document, create it under IAM > Policies, attach it to the role, then delete the inline version. Managed policies are versioned, reusable, and visible in one place.

rules.name: IAM Role Attached Policies
rules.description: IAM Roles should use least privilege policies. Review attached policies for excessive permissions.
rules.remediation: Review the policies attached to this role and remove permissions it does not use. IAM Access Analyzer can generate a policy from the role's recent CloudTrail activity, which is a far better starting point than trimming by hand.

rules.name: IAM User with AdministratorAccess Policy
rules.description: IAM Users should not have AdministratorAccess policy attached. Use least privilege principles and assign users to groups with appropriate permissions.
rules.remediation: Detach AdministratorAccess from the user. Give them a scoped policy covering their actual work, or a role they assume when admin is genuinely needed — standing admin on a user is what turns one stolen credential into a full account compromise.

rules.name: IAM User with FullAccess Managed Policy
rules.description: IAM Users should not have managed policies ending in 'FullAccess' attached. These policies grant full access to AWS services and violate least privilege principles.
rules.remediation: Detach the *FullAccess policy and grant only the actions needed. AWS publishes narrower managed policies for most services (ReadOnly, or specific job functions); start from one of those rather than from FullAccess.

rules.name: IAM User with Wildcard Policies
rules.description: IAM Users with inline policies may contain wildcard permissions (*) that grant full access to one or more services. Inline policies should be reviewed for least privilege compliance.
rules.remediation: Rewrite the inline policy to name specific actions and resources instead of using '*'. Check the user's CloudTrail history to see what is actually called, then move the result into a customer managed policy.

rules.name: S3 Public Access Block
rules.description: S3 Buckets should not be publicly available
rules.remediation: Enable Public Access Block on the bucket to prevent accidental public access.
rules.condition: $data === false || !isset($data['PublicAccessBlockConfiguration']) || ($data['PublicAccessBlockConfiguration']['BlockPublicAcls'] ?? false) == false || ($data['PublicAccessBlockConfiguration']['BlockPublicPolicy'] ?? false) == false || ($data['PublicAccessBlockConfiguration']['IgnorePublicAcls'] ?? false) == false || ($data['PublicAccessBlockConfiguration']['RestrictPublicBuckets'] ?? false) == false

rules.name: S3 Bucket Encryption
rules.description: S3 Buckets should have encryption enabled
rules.remediation: Enable server-side encryption (SSE) on the bucket.

rules.name: S3 Bucket versioning
rules.description: S3 Buckets should have versioning enabled
rules.remediation: Enable versioning on the bucket to protect against accidental deletion.

rules.name: S3 Bucket ACL Public Access
rules.description: S3 Bucket ACL should not allow public access
rules.remediation: Remove the public grants from the bucket ACL: S3 > bucket > Permissions > Access control list > Edit, and clear any grant to 'Everyone' or 'Authenticated users'. Then enable Block Public Access so it cannot be re-added. If the content is meant to be public, serve it through CloudFront with the bucket kept private.

rules.name: EC2 Security Group Allows Public Access
rules.description: EC2 Security Groups should not allow inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0
rules.remediation: Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 inbound rule from the security group and replace it with the specific CIDR ranges that need access. For administrative access prefer Systems Manager Session Manager, which requires no inbound rule at all.
rules.condition: isset($data['SecurityGroups']) && count(array_filter($data['SecurityGroups'] ?? [], function($sg) { return isset($sg['IpPermissions']) && count(array_filter($sg['IpPermissions'] ?? [], function($perm) { return isset($perm['IpRanges']) && count(array_filter($perm['IpRanges'] ?? [], function($range) { return ($range['CidrIp'] ?? '') == '0.0.0.0/0'; })) > 0; })) > 0; })) > 0

rules.name: EC2 Public IP Address
rules.description: EC2 Instances should not have a Public IP Address
rules.remediation: Consider using a NAT Gateway or removing the public IP if not needed.

rules.name: EC2 Default VPC in Use
rules.description: Default VPCs should not be used in production environments
rules.remediation: Move production workloads into a purpose-built VPC with subnets and routing you have chosen deliberately. The default VPC ships with public subnets and an open default security group, so it rarely matches what a production workload should have.
rules.condition: isset($data['Vpcs']) && count(array_filter($data['Vpcs'] ?? [], function($vpc) { return ($vpc['IsDefault'] ?? false) == true; })) > 0

rules.name: Subnet Default Public IP
rules.description: EC2 Subnets should not have Public IP enabled by default
rules.remediation: Disable auto-assign public IPv4 on the subnet: VPC > Subnets > Edit subnet settings. Instances needing outbound access should sit in a private subnet behind a NAT gateway; inbound traffic belongs on a load balancer.

rules.name: EC2 Instance Without Termination Protection
rules.description: EC2 Instances should have termination protection enabled for production workloads
rules.remediation: Enable termination protection: EC2 > instance > Actions > Instance settings > Change termination protection. It only guards against accidental termination through the API and console, so treat it as one layer rather than a backup strategy.

rules.name: RDS Instance Publicly Accessible
rules.description: RDS Instances should not be publicly accessible
rules.remediation: Set Public access to No: RDS > database > Modify > Connectivity, and tighten the security group to the application's group rather than a CIDR. Connect from inside the VPC via a bastion, VPN, or Session Manager port forwarding.

rules.name: RDS Instance Without Encryption
rules.description: RDS Instances should have encryption enabled
rules.remediation: Encryption cannot be turned on in place. Snapshot the instance, copy the snapshot with encryption enabled, restore from the copy, repoint the application, then delete the unencrypted original once you have verified the new one.

rules.name: RDS Instance Without Multi-AZ
rules.description: RDS Instances should have Multi-AZ enabled for production workloads
rules.remediation: Enable Multi-AZ: RDS > database > Modify > Availability & durability. Failover is automatic and typically completes in a minute or two; the modification itself can be applied in the next maintenance window to avoid an immediate restart.

rules.name: RDS Instance Without Backup Retention
rules.description: RDS Instances should have automated backups enabled with appropriate retention period
rules.remediation: Set a backup retention period of at least 7 days: RDS > database > Modify > Backup. Retention of 0 disables automated backups entirely and with it point-in-time recovery, so a mistake becomes unrecoverable.

rules.name: RDS Cluster Without Encryption
rules.description: RDS Clusters should have encryption enabled
rules.remediation: Encryption cannot be enabled on an existing cluster. Take a cluster snapshot, copy it with encryption enabled, restore a new cluster from the copy, repoint your application, then remove the unencrypted cluster.

rules.name: RDS Cluster Without Backup Retention
rules.description: RDS Clusters should have automated backups enabled with appropriate retention period
rules.remediation: Set a backup retention period of at least 7 days on the cluster: RDS > cluster > Modify > Backup. Retention of 0 means no automated backups and no point-in-time recovery.

rules.name: RDS Instance Without Deletion Protection
rules.description: RDS Instances should have deletion protection enabled for production workloads
rules.remediation: Enable deletion protection on the RDS instance.

rules.name: RDS Instance Without Enhanced Monitoring
rules.description: RDS Instances should have enhanced monitoring enabled for OS-level metrics
rules.remediation: Enable Enhanced Monitoring on the RDS instance for OS-level metrics.

rules.name: RDS Instance Without Auto Minor Version Upgrade
rules.description: RDS Instances should enable automatic minor version upgrades to receive security patches
rules.remediation: Enable automatic minor version upgrades on the RDS instance.

rules.name: EC2 Instance Metadata Service v1 Enabled
rules.description: EC2 Instances should enforce IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=required) to mitigate SSRF-based credential theft
rules.remediation: Set the instance metadata options to require IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=required).

rules.name: VPC Without Flow Logs
rules.description: Every VPC should have flow logs enabled to record network traffic for security analysis
rules.remediation: Enable VPC Flow Logs for the VPC and deliver them to CloudWatch Logs or S3.

rules.name: S3 Bucket Access Logging Disabled
rules.description: S3 Buckets should have server access logging enabled for audit and investigation
rules.remediation: Enable S3 server access logging and direct logs to a dedicated log bucket.

rules.name: Root Account MFA Disabled
rules.description: The AWS root account must have multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled
rules.remediation: Enable MFA on the AWS root account immediately and store the device securely.

rules.name: Root Account Access Keys Present
rules.description: The AWS root account should not have access keys; remove them and use IAM roles or users instead
rules.remediation: Delete the root account access keys and use IAM roles or IAM Identity Center instead.

rules.name: IAM Password Policy Weak Or Missing
rules.description: The account should enforce a strong IAM password policy with a minimum length of at least 14 characters
rules.remediation: Configure an IAM password policy with a minimum length of at least 14 characters and complexity requirements.

rules.name: CloudTrail Trail Not Logging
rules.description: CloudTrail trails should be actively logging to capture account activity
rules.remediation: Start logging on the CloudTrail trail so account activity is captured.

rules.name: CloudTrail Log File Validation Disabled
rules.description: CloudTrail log file validation should be enabled to detect tampering with log files
rules.remediation: Enable log file validation on the trail to detect tampering.

rules.name: CloudTrail Trail Not Multi-Region
rules.description: CloudTrail trails should be multi-region to capture activity across all regions
rules.remediation: Recreate or update the trail as a multi-region trail.

rules.name: CloudTrail Not Integrated With CloudWatch Logs
rules.description: CloudTrail should deliver logs to CloudWatch Logs for real-time monitoring and alerting
rules.remediation: Configure the trail to deliver events to a CloudWatch Logs log group.

rules.name: CloudTrail Logs Not Encrypted With KMS
rules.description: CloudTrail log files should be encrypted at rest using a KMS customer managed key
rules.remediation: Configure the trail to encrypt log files with a KMS customer managed key.

rules.name: Lambda Function URL Without Authentication
rules.description: Lambda function URLs should require IAM authentication; AuthType NONE exposes the function publicly
rules.remediation: Change the function URL AuthType to AWS_IAM, or remove the function URL if not required.

rules.name: Lambda Deprecated Runtime
rules.description: Lambda functions should not use deprecated runtimes, which no longer receive security updates
rules.remediation: Migrate the function to a currently supported runtime version.

rules.name: Lambda Function Without VPC Configuration
rules.description: Sensitive Lambda functions should run inside a VPC to restrict network access
rules.remediation: Attach a VPC configuration to the function if it accesses private resources.

rules.name: Lambda Environment Variable May Contain Secret
rules.description: Lambda environment variables named like secrets may store credentials in plaintext; use AWS Secrets Manager instead
rules.remediation: Move secrets out of environment variables into AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store.

rules.name: KMS Key Scheduled For Deletion
rules.description: KMS keys pending deletion will permanently destroy the ability to decrypt data encrypted under them
rules.remediation: Cancel the scheduled key deletion if the key is still needed for decryption.

rules.name: KMS Key Rotation Disabled
rules.description: Customer managed KMS keys should have automatic annual key rotation enabled
rules.remediation: Enable automatic key rotation on the customer managed KMS key.

rules.name: KMS Customer Key Disabled
rules.description: Disabled customer managed KMS keys cannot be used and may indicate misconfiguration
rules.remediation: Re-enable the KMS key if it is still required, or schedule it for deletion if not.

rules.name: SQS Queue Not Encrypted At Rest
rules.description: SQS queues should encrypt messages at rest using either an SQS-managed key or a KMS key.
rules.remediation: Enable server-side encryption on the queue, using SQS-managed encryption (SSE-SQS) or a KMS customer managed key.

rules.name: SNS Topic Not Encrypted At Rest
rules.description: SNS topics should encrypt messages at rest using a KMS key.
rules.remediation: Set a KMS master key on the topic to enable server-side encryption.

rules.name: DynamoDB Point-In-Time Recovery Disabled
rules.description: DynamoDB tables should have point-in-time recovery enabled so data can be restored after accidental writes or deletes.
rules.remediation: Enable point-in-time recovery on the table.

rules.name: DynamoDB Deletion Protection Disabled
rules.description: Production DynamoDB tables should have deletion protection enabled to prevent accidental removal.
rules.remediation: Enable deletion protection on the table.

rules.name: Load Balancer Listener Without TLS
rules.description: Load balancer listeners should terminate TLS rather than serving plaintext HTTP.
rules.remediation: Replace the HTTP listener with an HTTPS listener, or redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

rules.name: Load Balancer Access Logging Disabled
rules.description: Load balancers should write access logs to S3 for incident investigation.
rules.remediation: Enable access logging on the load balancer and point it at a dedicated log bucket.
